title: Regressive Prediction of Focused Ion Beam Milling Depth for Electron Diffraction Gratings
content: Electron diffraction gratings have introduced a new regime of interferometric measurement capabilities to the transmission electron microscope (TEM). The first demonstration of electron interaction free measurement utilized two gratings to construct a Mach-Zehnder interferometer in a TEM [1]. A similar two grating apparatus was utilized to carry out inelastic interferometric measurements which mapped the electrostatic potential surrounding a metallic nanoparticle [2]. Single electron diffraction grating holography has even measured small phase shifts introduced by low atomic number elements while maintaining atomic resolution [3]. Focused ion beams (FIBs) present unparalleled simplicity and control as a nanofabrication platform for these electron optical elements. However, electron diffraction gratings require FIB milling depth accuracy of single nanometers to optimize electron current in each diffractive probe [4]. Therefore, precision in grating fabrication is paramount. Here we present a data-based regression model that predicts the FIB milling depth of silicon nitride membrane electron diffraction gratings with a precision of several nanometers
